review_provenance.independent_from: parent implementation/architecture agent and prior W1 authoring pass
review_provenance.blinding: NOT_BLINDED: W1 verdicts read, then independently compared against population claims and canonical competencies
review_provenance.method: Deterministic Python joins and counts; bounded semantic coverage judgments by the separate audit agent. No external LLM API, no question generation and no packet repair.
review_provenance.clinical_scope: Artifact-to-competency alignment only. No assertion that transcription verification establishes medical correctness, source entailment or current legal/clinical validity.

state_definitions.ALIGNED_COMPLETE: All declared address competencies have direct evidence at their stated level; does not mean generation-ready or that all possible item facts are supplied.
state_definitions.ALIGNED_PARTIAL: Only bounded in-topic decision content or identified prerequisites are supported. Unsupported content remains blocked; PREREQUISITE_ONLY is not an admissible learner decision.
state_definitions.MISALIGNED: The actual researched claims target another topic, population or decision, with no supported address decision.
state_definitions.EVIDENCE_MISSING: Required packet or usable claim evidence absent.

decision_support_policy: Never promote an entire ALIGNED_PARTIAL address. Only an explicitly scoped learner decision can advance after checking its own required claims, entailment and currentness. PREREQUISITE_ONLY rows cannot advance on this audit alone.

prior_scope_errors: W1 called SU-C-35 recognition/confirmation its declared competency; canonical competency is comparison with restrictive cardiomyopathy.
W1 described SU-PH-08 as community needs assessment; canonical competencies are Ottawa Charter, behaviour-change models and risk versus harm reduction.
W1 omitted the mortality-rate competency in SU-PH-10.
W1 collapsed PH-41 components to parent content; this audit uses the six component scopes, including births/stillbirths and flying safety.
W1 described PM-06 as ACP/code-status coverage without checking the actual terminology and timing competency text.

uncertainties: A partial row can still support a useful narrowly scoped decision; this is not an estimate of safe question yield.
Completeness is judged at the declared competency level rather than encyclopedic topic completeness.
No live legal/medical assertions were reverified; high-freshness claims need currentness review before use.

Canonical competency wording itself is not adjudicated clinical evidence. In particular no recommendation is made from PM-06 CPR/DNR generalizations, PH-11 statistical error wording or PH-10 summary scale wording.
All 45 addresses currently have populated packet evidence; evidence existence and plan-ID joins do not establish content alignment.

The canonical CPR/DNR wording is a scope statement, not newly validated medical guidance.
reviews.old_reason: The CMPA and CPSO packet covers advance care planning against contemporaneous consent, the goals-of-care discussion and the Ontario withhold-versus-withdraw distinction, matching the code-status and ACP competencies. It is the richest MED packet in the set.

canonical_testable_competencies.eligibility_pathways: Distinguish MAID Track 1 (natural death reasonably foreseeable) from Track 2 (serious and incurable illness/disease/disability, death not reasonably foreseeable) eligibility pathways.
canonical_testable_competencies.response_to_request: Respond to a patient's MAID request with a compassionate, non-judgmental approach and take appropriate steps toward referral if the patient meets eligibility criteria, recognizing the current mental-illness-sole-criterion exclusion.

reviewed_claims.statement: Respond to a MAID request without assuming eligibility: clarify that it is a voluntary patient request, assess decision-making capacity and freedom from external pressure, provide the information needed for informed consent including diagnosis, treatments and available means to relieve suffering such as palliative care, and connect the patient with the applicable provincial or territorial assessment pathway.

reviewed_claims.statement: Federal eligibility does not require a terminal condition, but every criterion must be met and two independent practitioners must confirm eligibility. When natural death is not reasonably foreseeable, the additional Track 2 safeguards include relevant-condition expertise or consultation, discussion of reasonable available means to relieve suffering, and a minimum 90-day assessment period unless assessments are complete and loss of capacity is imminent.

reviewed_claims.statement: A person whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness is not eligible for MAID before March 17, 2027; a person with mental illness plus another qualifying condition may still be individually assessed under the current criteria.

reviewed_claims.statement: A waiver of final consent is not a general advance request: federally it is available only after eligibility is established and, for clinician-administered MAID, when natural death is reasonably foreseeable and the statutory written arrangement is completed. Quebec separately permits advance requests under its provincial law as of October 30, 2024, creating a jurisdiction-specific situation requiring current local guidance.
